reasons: reads as a plain extruded bar
only one notch/entry event, no clear public void or terrace
does not establish a distinct section or threshold relation
too close to maas_01 in footprint and overall bar logic
step-back roof is not enough to make a new family
public-space language remains weak and decorative

rationale: This contact sheet is not yet a portfolio: only two visible candidates and both belong to the same compact bar family. The apparent differences are limited to a stepped upper profile versus a smoother one, but the footprint, overall chassis, and front notch logic are shared. For this program, the missing requirement is not polish but a clear three-dimensional language of public threshold and usable void. The next iteration needs genuinely different spatial families—courtyard, bent bar, split wing, carved terrace, lifted mass—so the active ground edge and program-specific public space read immediately.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: Both read as the same compact bar/block mass family with a single front notch and a calm upper cap; the second only stair-steps the same chassis rather than establishing a new spatial idea.

required_next_relations: Introduce at least one courtyard or carve_void family that makes a usable public pocket at the ground edge.
Add a bent_bar or split_wing relation that changes the street threshold and not just the roofline.
Vary section through lift/cantilever/bridge so upper mass clearly differs from a calm base without repeating the same bar chassis.
Make at least 10 materially legible families across the 20-option set; keep any single family under 30%.
Preserve west-facing active frontage while tying the void/terrace to mixed-use ground program, not decorative subtraction.
